title: Extension Types for Free
summary: Extension types are a concept in dependent type theory that has appeared in various contexts. The idea is to have types whose terms are partially determined, e.g. via a strict boundary condition. Standard examples are path types of cubical type theories (paths with fixed endpoints), Riehl and Shulman's name-giving extension types (terms fixed on subshapes), as well as the controlled-unfolding mechanism of cooltt and Agda (terms that are fixed if a condition is met).
